title: firewalld and iptables
subtitle: Zones, services, panic, masquerade, and port forwarding

cards.meaning: Dynamically managed firewall daemon using zones for trust levels
cards.notes: Supports IPv4/IPv6, bridges, IP sets, runtime vs permanent, and apps adding rules without hand-editing iptables.

cards.meaning: Trust level bound to an interface (or source); decides open services, NAT, etc.
cards.notes: Zone = how much do I trust this NIC / this network?

cards.meaning: Runtime = active now; permanent = XML on disk for after reboot/--reload
cards.notes: --permanent then --reload copies disk → runtime. Runtime-only changes vanish on reload.

cards.meaning: Old iptables-service config: one big IPv4 (and IPv6) rule dump
cards.notes: system-config-firewall GUI wrote the same files.

cards.meaning: firewalld XML: stock defaults in /usr/lib; your overrides in /etc
cards.notes: Zones, services, and more under /etc/firewalld/.

cards.meaning: Normal when firewalld is default — the old file often does not exist
cards.notes: Only look for it if you switched back to the iptables service.

cards.front: How iptables service applies a change
cards.meaning: Flush all old rules, reread entire file, rebuild from scratch
cards.notes: Tears down the firewall briefly and typically drops existing connections.

cards.meaning: Only differences are applied; existing connections can stay up
cards.notes: iptables service = throw away the wall; firewalld = add/remove one brick.

cards.meaning: Kernel packet filter; firewalld or iptables service programs it
cards.notes: The iptables command may still display the resulting chains.

cards.meaning: Lowest trust: all incoming dropped with no reply; outgoing still possible
cards.notes: Remote side sees silence (timeout), not a rejection.

cards.meaning: Incoming rejected with ICMP error (icmp-host-prohibited / icmp6-adm-prohibited)
cards.notes: Client is told “no,” instead of hanging.

cards.meaning: IPv4 reject message used by the block zone
cards.notes: IPv6 counterpart: icmp6-adm-prohibited.

cards.meaning: Untrusted networks; allow only selected incoming (e.g. ssh, maybe http)
cards.notes: Default zone on many servers (internet, café Wi-Fi).

cards.meaning: Gateway WAN side; configured for NAT masquerading
cards.notes: Internal RFC1918 stays private; hosts reachable via firewall’s public IP.

cards.meaning: Gateway LAN side; fairly trustworthy, more services than public/external
cards.notes: Pair with external for NAT gateway.

cards.meaning: Isolated hosts with no access to the rest of the network; limited incoming
cards.notes: e.g. a public web server in a separate segment.

cards.meaning: Office LAN — trust most computers; a few more services than public
Home LAN — trust most; a few more services accepted
Most open: trust all machines; almost no incoming filtering
cards.notes: Use sparingly (lab, fully private segment).

cards.meaning: Port + protocol (+ sometimes a kernel helper) so you allow ftp instead of 21/tcp by hand
cards.notes: --get-services = menu.

cards.meaning: List named services you can allow (ssh, http, ftp, …)
Show ports/modules for that named service
cards.notes: ftp → ports: 21/tcp; modules: nf_conntrack_ftp.

cards.meaning: Control channel 21/tcp
Kernel helper so related FTP data ports can be tracked
cards.notes: Shown by --info-service=ftp.

cards.meaning: Drop all packets immediately (global emergency lock)
cards.notes: Not a zone. Can lock you out of SSH — use --panic-off from console if needed.

cards.meaning: Leave panic mode
Leaving packets get the firewall’s IP as source; replies un-NAT to the real internal host
cards.notes: Use internal (LAN) + external (internet); turn masquerade on external.

cards.meaning: Enable NAT masquerade on external (runtime — temporary)
cards.notes: Masquerade on external, not internal. Gone after reboot/firewall restart unless permanent.

cards.meaning: Turn masquerading off for the zone
Ask whether masquerade is active in this zone
Survive reboot: write XML under /etc/firewalld/, then load into runtime
cards.notes: --permanent alone does not change live rules until --reload (or restart).

cards.meaning: Load permanent config into runtime
cards.notes: Runtime-only changes vanish on reload unless also made permanent.

cards.meaning: DNAT: send inbound traffic for a port to another internal address or alternate port
cards.notes: Requires masquerading — classic RHCE exam mistake.

cards.meaning: Forward inbound port to another port (same host unless toaddr= set)
cards.notes: port= seen on firewall; proto= protocol; toport= where sent. Masquerade first.

cards.meaning: Seen port; protocol; destination port; optional destination address
cards.notes: Without toaddr=, forward stays on the same host.
